evidence.description: Repository-relative paths of files that were actually read and that support the statement they are attached to. Everything downstream treats a stack fact as a fact only because of these; a claim with nothing behind it is a guess, and a guess about the product's language is how automation ends up written in something nobody on the team maintains.

componentStack.description: What one component is built out of, read from its own manifests rather than inferred from file extensions.

role.description: Only components marked product decide the repository's primary stack. Test and tooling components are recorded because existing automation is the first thing the architect should try to extend, but a repository whose only JavaScript is a build script is not a JavaScript product.

runtime.description: The SDK or runtime version the component pins - a global.json SDK, a TargetFramework, an engines range. Absent when nothing in the repository pins one.

dependencies.description: Direct dependencies as declared, not as resolved. Enough of them to recognise the frameworks in use; not the transitive closure.

testFrameworks.description: Test frameworks this component already runs. An empty array means none were found, which is a different answer from not having looked - say so in unknowns if the component was not readable.

ciEnvironment.description: What the pipelines already install and run for this component - an SDK version, a node version, a container image. Automation that needs something the agents do not have is automation that never runs.

packageFeeds.description: The feeds this component restores from, as configured. A repository that restores from a private feed cannot be automated against the public one.

primaryStack.description: The stack the repository is actually written in. This is the architect's starting candidate for the automation, so it is decided from what the product components are built out of and what the repository exists to do - never from a file count, which vendored code and generated output win.

ecosystem.description: The package ecosystem the primary stack restores from, named as the ecosystem rather than the tool: npm, nuget, maven.

polyglot.description: True when product components are genuinely built in more than one stack, which changes the architect's question from which language to which component's language.

excludedFromStackDetermination.description: Paths deliberately left out of the primary-stack answer, each with the reason. Vendored dependencies, generated output and the automation installation's own directory are all code in the repository and none of them says anything about what the product is written in.
